products.name: Real-Time CDP
products.what: Helps companies bring together known and anonymous data from multiple enterprise sources in order to create customer profiles that can be used to provide personalized customer experiences across all channels and devices in real time.

lines.name: Data model, schema and identity design
lines.scope: Run use-case workshops, map the client's entities into profile, event and lookup schemas, and choose the identity namespaces and primary identities the profile will merge on.
lines.evidence: it is important to follow best practices for data modeling when designing your schemas

lines.name: Data sources and ingestion setup
lines.scope: Connect the agreed sources such as CRM, loyalty, commerce and web or app events, map fields to XDM, enable datasets for Profile and check that the first loads build the expected profiles.
lines.evidence: You can ingest data from a variety of sources such as Adobe applications, cloud-based storages, databases, and many others.

lines.name: Profile and merge policy configuration
lines.scope: Set the merge method and dataset priority in the default merge policy, review how the identity graph links records, and check sample profiles against source data.
lines.evidence: merge policies are the rules that Experience Platform uses to determine how data will be prioritized

lines.name: Audience build and destination activation
lines.scope: Build the starting audiences, connect the agreed destinations, choose the identities and attributes to send, then schedule and test the first activations.
lines.evidence: After you configure your destination, you can activate audiences in multiple ways

lines.name: Governance, access and sandbox setup
lines.scope: Set up roles, permissions and development and production sandboxes, apply data usage labels and policies to datasets, and confirm activations respect those policies.
lines.evidence: assist your team with the right permissions, access controls, and sandbox configurations

lines.name: Monthly audience and dataflow operations
lines.scope: Each month, review source and destination dataflows and alerts, fix failed runs, retire or refresh audiences, and add destinations as new use cases come in.
lines.evidence: Experience Platform allows you to track how data is being processed through the use of dataflows

source.title: Adobe Experience Platform end-to-end example workflow

products.name: Journey Optimizer
products.what: Builds on Adobe Experience Platform to connect customer data, content creation, and journey orchestration in a single, continuous system.

lines.name: Access, sandbox and channel setup
lines.scope: Set up roles and sandboxes, delegate the sending subdomains, and create the email and other channel configurations, IP pools and suppression and allowed lists.
lines.evidence: Define all the technical parameters required for email, mobile messages, push notifications, web push, direct mail, and other channels

lines.name: Journey events, data sources and actions
lines.scope: Configure the identity namespaces, profile-enabled schemas and datasets the journeys need, then the journey events, data sources, custom actions and test profiles.
lines.evidence: to be able to send messages in journeys, you must configure Data Sources, Events and Actions

lines.name: IP warmup plan execution
lines.scope: Create the warmup campaigns, load the warmup plan, run each phase and watch delivery and reputation signals until sending volume reaches its target.
lines.evidence: To avoid being marked as spam, you can progressively increase the volume sent using the IP warmup plan feature.

source.title: Get started with IP warmup plans

lines.name: Content templates and personalization
lines.scope: Build reusable email and message templates and fragments, set up personalization and dynamic content, and preview rendering with test profiles.
lines.evidence: Create reusable content templates and fragments to maintain brand consistency.

lines.name: First journeys and campaigns
lines.scope: Design, build, test and publish the starting journeys and campaigns, such as a welcome series, an abandoned cart journey and a scheduled campaign, with entry, wait and exit rules.
lines.evidence: Build multi-step customer journeys to initiate a sequence of interactions, offers, and messages across channels in real time.

lines.name: Monthly journey operations and optimization
lines.scope: Each month, review journey and campaign reports, fix errors and bottlenecks, run content experiments, and tune frequency and quiet hours rules.
lines.evidence: Monitor and optimize. Track performance and improve results over time

products.name: Target
products.what: Offers comprehensive tools to personalize customer experiences across web, mobile sites, apps, social media, and other digital channels.

lines.name: Target implementation with Web SDK
lines.scope: Enable Target in the datastream, add flicker handling, render Visual and Form-based Experience Composer activities, pass profile and entity data, and validate the setup.
lines.evidence: Configure a datastream to enable Target functionality

source.title: Set up Adobe Target with Platform Web SDK

lines.name: Users, workspaces and audiences setup
lines.scope: Add users and roles, create workspaces and properties where the client has Target Premium, and set up the reporting, environment and starting audience settings.
lines.evidence: create workspaces, user groups, and properties; update your Target implementation to include the at_property parameter

lines.name: Testing roadmap and first activities
lines.scope: Run an ideation and prioritization workshop, write activity plans with hypotheses and success metrics, then build, QA and launch the first A/B and Experience Targeting activities.
lines.evidence: Rank and schedule activities based on business alignment, level of effort, and potential impact.

source.title: Chapter 3: Develop your testing and personalization ideas

lines.name: Recommendations catalog and setup
lines.scope: Set up the product or content catalog feed, pass item, category and cart data on key pages, set global exclusions and Recommendations settings, and launch the first recommendations.
lines.evidence: Set up your Recommendations catalog of products or content that you want to recommend to your users.

lines.name: Monthly test design, build and analysis
lines.scope: Each month, design, build, QA and launch the next activities on the roadmap, analyze results by audience, and share readouts and next steps with stakeholders.
lines.evidence: establish a formal, repeatable process for coming up with ideas for testing and personalization activities

source.title: Chapter 3: Develop your testing and personalization ideas

products.name: Customer Journey Analytics
products.what: Adobe's next-generation Analytics solution that lets you use the power of Analysis Workspace with data from Adobe Experience Platform.

lines.name: CJA data preparation in Experience Platform
lines.scope: Design the XDM schemas, create the datasets and set up ingestion for the channels CJA will report on, such as web, app, call center and point of sale data.
lines.evidence: Use Adobe Experience Data Model (XDM) to standardize customer experience data and define schemas

lines.name: Connections, data views and stitching
lines.scope: Create the connection with the right person ID for each dataset, turn on field-based or graph-based stitching in the connection where needed, and build data views with the client's components and settings.
lines.evidence: A connection lets you integrate datasets from Adobe Experience Platform into Workspace.

lines.name: Adobe Analytics upgrade to CJA
lines.scope: Plan the upgrade path, implement Web SDK alongside the Analytics source connector for history, port reporting API use and exports, and migrate projects and components.
lines.evidence: a new implementation of the Experience Platform Web SDK, which is the preferred data collection method

source.title: Upgrade from Adobe Analytics to Customer Journey Analytics

lines.name: Workspace projects and dashboards
lines.scope: Build the starting Analysis Workspace projects and dashboards for each team's priority questions, with cross-channel journeys, KPIs and segments.
lines.evidence: analyze the data you have brought in using the power and flexibility of Analysis Workspace

lines.name: User onboarding and training
lines.scope: Plan role-based onboarding, train users on Analysis Workspace and on what differs from Adobe Analytics, and set up shared components and templates.
lines.evidence: give your users ample time (3 - 6 months) to become familiar with the key differences

lines.name: Monthly journey analysis and insights
lines.scope: Each month, run flow, fallout and attribution analysis on priority journeys, report findings to stakeholders and recommend next actions.
lines.evidence: Advanced analysis leverages features like Flow diagrams, Attribution, Fallout diagrams, and dimension breakdowns.

connections.how: Both apps read the same Experience Platform data: audience analysis brings Real-Time CDP audience membership from Profile datasets into a CJA connection as new dimensions, and audience publishing sends CJA audiences back to Real-Time Customer Profile.

lines.name: Real-Time CDP audience analysis in CJA
lines.scope: Configure audience analysis by choosing the sandbox, merge policy, connection and data views (Adobe then creates the lookup dataset, audience dimensions and data view settings), and extend Adobe's Audience overview template with the client's KPIs.
lines.evidence: Audience analysis allows you to ingest audience membership data from Experience Platform Profile datasets into a Customer Journey Analytics connection.

lines.name: Identity and audience count alignment
lines.scope: Align the CJA person ID and stitching method with the Real-Time CDP identity graph, agree which datasets and retention windows each app uses, and document expected audience count differences for stakeholders.
lines.evidence: Real-time CDP and Customer Journey Analytics do not share the same definition of a person today.

source.title: Consistency of metrics and audience membership

connections.how: Journey Optimizer data lands in Experience Platform datasets, and when CJA reporting is enabled for Journey Optimizer, Adobe automatically creates a connection and data view for the sandbox.

lines.name: Journey data in the main CJA connection
lines.scope: Add the Journey Optimizer datasets to the client's main CJA connection with web, app and offline data in a separate data view, leaving Adobe's auto-created connection and data view untouched so Journey Optimizer's own reports keep working.
lines.evidence: Or you can add Journey Optimizer datasets to an existing connection.

lines.name: Journey and experiment analysis in CJA
lines.scope: Build Workspace projects that tie journeys and messages to web, app and offline conversions, plus Experimentation panel reports for journey content experiments.
lines.evidence: Customer Journey Analytics data views and analysis provide campaign and journey insight.

source.title: Adobe Customer Journey Analytics & Adobe Journey Optimizer integration

connections.how: A Target activity that uses CJA as its reporting source sends its data to Experience Platform (Web SDK is the preferred method), Adobe creates the Adobe Target Classification Events lookup dataset, and activity reports are built in CJA.

source.title: Target reporting in Adobe Customer Journey Analytics

lines.name: Target reporting setup in CJA
lines.scope: Add the event dataset and the Adobe Target Classification Events lookup dataset (created by Adobe) to a CJA connection, then add activity and experience dimensions with persistence and the Experimentation context labels.
lines.evidence: configure persistence for the Activity Name and Activity ID dimensions

source.title: Target reporting in Adobe Customer Journey Analytics

lines.name: Experiment reports in Workspace
lines.scope: Build Experimentation panel reports and a reusable Workspace template for Target activities, showing lift and confidence on the client's CJA success metrics.
lines.evidence: Activity reports must be built in Customer Journey Analytics.

source.title: Target reporting in Adobe Customer Journey Analytics

lines.name: A4T to CJA reporting transition
lines.scope: For clients on Analytics for Target today, choose which activity types move to CJA reporting, set the reporting source per activity or account wide, and give Target users the Experience Platform role they need.
lines.evidence: This functionality is comparable to what is performed in Adobe Analytics (AA) via Analytics for Target (A4T)

bv_so_direct_integration.explanation: Adobe markets the two together but documents no product-to-product integration. Adobe's brand visibility solutions page lists Sites Optimizer and Brand Visibility in one suite ('Together, these products cover every stage of brand visibility') and an Ultimate Success webinar covers combining them, but the Brand Visibility docs, Optimize at Edge page and release notes never mention Sites Optimizer, and the Sites Optimizer docs, settings (Google Search Console and Connect to AEM Sites only) and release notes never mention Brand Visibility or LLM Optimizer. The two security overviews don't mention each other either; both list Adobe IMS sign-in, the AEM Experience Hub and AEM operational telemetry, which are shared Adobe services rather than a link between the two products. The Brand Visibility product page names its native integrations as Adobe Analytics and Customer Journey Analytics.

notes: Hours are our own estimates for a mid-market client (low, base, high). Adobe publishes no hours for any of this work. Quantities in the scopes, such as starting journeys, audiences or activities, are illustrative and not Adobe recommendations.

Shared Experience Platform foundation: Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer and CJA sit on the same schemas, datasets, identities, sandboxes and permissions, and Adobe's Data Architect tutorial says Platform services are 'critical foundations of those applications'. When more than one of the three is on the canvas, count RT01, RT02, RT05, the schema and dataset part of JO02, the sandbox and role part of JO01, and CJ01 once. They fit the canvas idea of work counted once per engagement.

Web SDK is shared: Adobe's CJA upgrade page recommends one Web SDK implementation and lists 'Consolidate implementation for Adobe CX Enterprise data collection' across AJO and Real-Time CDP. TG01, the web part of RT02 and CJ03 should not each pay for the same tags and datastream; use the low end of whichever comes second.

Adobe builds the Journey Optimizer to CJA plumbing itself: enabling CJA reporting for Journey Optimizer automatically creates the AJO Enabled Connection and its data view for each sandbox, and Adobe warns that editing them affects Journey Optimizer reporting. Journey Optimizer's built-in reports run on CJA even for clients who don't own CJA, so the JC lines apply only when the client owns CJA and wants analysis beyond those reports.

Other work Adobe does automatically: the Adobe Target Classification Events lookup dataset (created once an activity reports to CJA); audience analysis creates its lookup dataset, audience dimensions and data view settings, and Adobe ships an Audience overview template; publishing a CJA audience creates the streaming segment in Real-Time CDP; with full subdomain delegation (Adobe's recommended method) Adobe configures the DNS records for Journey Optimizer. Stitching no longer needs an Adobe support request; it is turned on in the CJA Connections UI.

The existing catalog line C06, Audiences that act on the data (CJA audiences published to Real-Time CDP), also belongs on the Real-Time CDP and CJA connection, and it is how CJA audiences reach Journey Optimizer. It is not repeated here.

Target reporting in CJA is not A4T: there is no pre-built report, one reporting source per activity, the source can't change after go-live, and Auto-Target and Automated Personalization activities don't support CJA reporting yet. Web SDK is the preferred implementation; an Analytics source connection is the fallback.

Target Premium features: Recommendations, properties and workspaces (enterprise permissions), Auto-Target and Automated Personalization. For a Target Standard client, TG02 shrinks to users and audiences and TG04 drops out.
CJA packaging: Adobe's stitching page says field-based stitching needs the CJA Select package or higher and graph-based stitching needs Prime or higher.

Journey Optimizer IP warmup runs only on production sandboxes, and Adobe's page says the warmup sheet is prepared with the help of the client's deliverability consultant, so JO03 covers running the plan, not writing it.

Real-Time CDP and CJA numbers will differ: Adobe says consistency of metrics and audience membership across the two cannot be guaranteed (different person definitions, datasets, retention and latency). RC02 sets expectations rather than promising matching counts.

Gap between Adobe pages: CJA's integrations overview lists Adobe Analytics, Target, Adobe Advertising, Journey Optimizer, Decision Management and Customer AI, but not Real-Time CDP. The Real-Time CDP link is documented on the audience analysis and audience publishing pages instead.
Small conflict on Adobe's CJA Journey Optimizer page: the auto-created data view is called AJO Enable Data View in the text and AJO Enabled Data View in the table.

Candidates: the two Brand Concierge integrations come from Adobe's product page on business.adobe.com, not Experience League; the Brand Concierge docs only say deep AEM, AEP and Commerce integrations speed setup. The Commerce and CJA candidate rests on the Commerce Data Connection page; no CJA-side Commerce guide was found.

Flag for the existing catalog, not changed: the Sites Optimizer settings page has a Connect to AEM Sites section for Edge Delivery sites (code repository plus content source access), a more specific source for SO1 than the opportunity types page it cites today.

business.adobe.com pages and adobe.com PDFs refuse direct downloads from the research machine, so they were read through a fetch tool and quoted as returned. Every Experience League quote in the lines was checked word for word against the downloaded page on Oct 30 2026.
